Nine injured, three critically, after Bangkok oil refinery explosion

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (320 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Watch: Fire and smoke billows out of refinery owned by energy company Bangchak Corporation.
  • Nine people have been injured after an explosion at an oil refinery in Bangkok, authorities have stated.
  • Three of them are in critical condition, according to news agency AFP, which mentioned the local hospital had revised its earlier assessment of four.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Watch: Fire and smoke billows out of refinery owned by energy company Bangchak Corporation.

Nine people have been injured after an explosion at an oil refinery in Bangkok, authorities have stated.

Three of them are in critical condition, according to news agency AFP, which mentioned the local hospital had revised its earlier assessment of four.

A fire broke out after the blast at the Phra Khanong facility run by energy giant Bangchak Corporation in the east of Thailand's capital at around 14:45 (07:45 GMT).

The company remarked the fire was brought under control and put out within 30 minutes, adding that the cause of the incident was being investigated.

Black smoke could be seen across Bangkok's skyline after the blast, as local officials told residents to leave the area.

An alert sent to mobile phones by Bangkok authorities confirmed that the fire was under control, but urged people to avoid the area.

Eyewitnesses shared video clips on social media of flames and smoke rising above the refinery.

On a visit to the scene, Thailand's energy minister Akanat Promphan said it appeared the impact of the explosion was limited because the fire started in a distillation tower about 100m (330ft) from where oil was being stored.

He said the incident was concerning as the refinery was in a residential area and the government was suspending production until it could be confident that operations would resume without any complications.

Bangchak Corporation said air quality monitoring in the immediate area around the refinery was within normal ranges.

It confirmed that production at the site, which can process up to 120,000 barrels of oil a day had been shut down. The company has a second refinery in Chonburi province, about 50 miles (80km) from Bangkok, handling a daily capacity of about 180,000 barrels.

An explosion occurred at the Bangkok refinery in July 2012, sparking a fire but no reported injuries.

    💡 Key Takeaways

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The current policy adds: “Under no circumstances do we rent, trade, or share your address or e-mail address with any other company for their marketing purposes without your consent.” It also makes no mention of advertisers.

    This has concerned some owners, but a Backblaze spokesperson told Ars Technica that “Backblaze does not sell or share sensory or surveillance data, such as call recordings, for targeted advertising, and we do not disclose it to advertising or marketing partners.” They added:.

    Notably, no “sensitive personal information,” such as social security numbers, credit card numbers, or “precise geolocation,” is shared with advertisers, the policy states. However, identifiers, commercial information, “Internet or Other Similar Network Activity,” and “geolocation data” may be “sold or shared for targeted Advertising”.

    Critically, the upcoming policy “only applies to the information collected in respect of your account and not to the content that you store on our system.” Backblaze’s broader terms of service also state that: “Files stored using Backblaze Computer Backup are encrypted prior to being sent to us.”.

    Renatta Siewert, Backblaze’s director of communications and brand programs, reiterated to Ars that Backblaze doesn’t share the contents of backup or storage files with advertisers:.

    According to recent reports, backblaze takes the privacy and security of our customers’ data seriously. We updated our Privacy Notice to keep pace with the changing legal landscape, which increasingly requires companies to spell out how they collect and use marketing-related information. This revision gives customers a clearer, more specific view of what we collect and why. These disclosures are separate from the files customers entrust to Backblaze for backup and storage, which we do not sell or share with advertisers, data brokers, or analytics partners.

    Customers can use this link to opt out of the selling or sharing of their personal information for cross-context behavioral advertising.

    SpaceX gets FCC approval to deploy 1 million satellites for its AI orbital data center

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (398 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Engadget

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The FCC expects the initiative, called Starmind, to deploy it first satellite by November 2033.
    • The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has approved SpaceX's request to deploy 1 million satellites to build its AI orbital data center.
    • In a recent development, but can space-based data centers for AI really work?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The FCC expects the initiative, called Starmind, to deploy it first satellite by November 2033.

    The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has approved SpaceX's request to deploy 1 million satellites to build its AI orbital data center. SpaceX filed its application at the beginning of the year, presenting the initiative called Starmind as the better alternative for ground-based data centers. In its filing, the company argued that "orbital data centers are the most efficient way to meet the accelerating demand for AI computing power," since they use "solar power with little operating and maintenance costs.".

    In a recent development, but can space-based data centers for AI really work? Critics doubt they can. Adam Becker, an astrophysicist and a critic of Elon Musk's space and AI ambitions, told AP that "it's not going to happen. The idea behind sending AI data centers outside our planet is so that they don't consume resources their ground-based counterparts do, like energy and water for cooling.

    Industry observers note that however, critics of the blueprint argue that space is a vacuum that traps heat inside objects and doesn't make cooling down hardware easier. In space, heat has to leave the satellites via radiation, and Becker explained that there are "basic physical limits" to radiating the heat out for all of them. In addition, that many satellites could cause in-orbit collisions and generate a huge amount of space junk.

    In a recent development, FCC Chairman Brendan Carr believes that with this approval, though, America is "leading the world into the era of super intelligence." It opens a "bold fresh frontier," he added. Under the terms the FCC has approved, SpaceX has permission to deploy satellites into orbital layers spanning 50 kilometers, at altitudes between 500 meters and 1,002 kilometers.

    The organization is required to deploy at lease one authorized satellite and place it into its assigned orbit by November 25, 2033. By the same date in 2035, it must have already deployed 100,000 satellites to their respective orbits. Three years later, on November 25, 2028, it must have already deployed 500,000 of the authorized satellites. All 1 million satellites must have already been placed in their assigned orbits no later than November 25, 2040. Musk previously noted that SpaceX will start launching the satellites in 2027, but we'll have to wait and see if the company can stick to that timeline.

    #151578. Duterte's ICC trial: What is at stake for the Philippines?

    Duterte's ICC trial: What is at stake for the Philippines?

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1204 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte will stand trial at the International Criminal Court (ICC) in The Hague on November 30, where he faces three counts of crimes against humanity linked to his bloody war on drugs.
    • For the families of the thousands killed during his anti-narcotics campaign, the trial is a chance for justice that has eluded them at home.
    • It is also a significant test of international justice at a time when the ICC faces increasing political pressure and questions about its ability to hold former heads of state accountable.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte will stand trial at the International Criminal Court (ICC) in The Hague on November 30, where he faces three counts of crimes against humanity linked to his bloody war on drugs.

    For the families of the thousands killed during his anti-narcotics campaign, the trial is a chance for justice that has eluded them at home.

    It is also a significant test of international justice at a time when the ICC faces increasing political pressure and questions about its ability to hold former heads of state accountable.

    Yet, Duterte, 81, is still a popular figure in the Philippines, where many still regard his violent crackdown as one of his presidency's greatest achievements.

    With his daughter, Vice President Sara Duterte, a frontrunner for the 2028 presidential election, the proceedings in The Hague could become a defining concern in the Philippines' next presidential election.

    Rodrigo Duterte was elected president in 2016 following an expletive-laden, populist campaign in which he openly promised to kill criminals and drug dealers.

    During his more than two decades as mayor of Davao City, he earned a reputation for transforming a notoriously violent city into a relatively safe one.

    To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

    However, human rights groups found systematic extrajudicial killings by the so-called Davao Death Squad, which ICC prosecutors allege Duterte helped establish and oversee.

    His disregard for political convention and promises of swift, uncompromising justice appealed to millions of Filipinos frustrated by corruption, crime and the perceived failures of successive governments.

    "Filipinos who were deeply frustrated with everyday experiences of injustice and government inaction made them receptive to Duterte's promise of swift justice, even though extraordinary and violent means," Cleve Arguelles, a political scientist and CEO of Momentum Research, a pollster, told DW.

    According to recent reports, after assuming the presidency, Duterte extended his Davao law enforcement model nationwide. Police debuted sweeping anti-narcotics operations, primarily targeting impoverished urban communities, while suspected drug people and dealers were also killed by unidentified gunmen.

    Philippine authorities officially recorded 6,252 deaths during anti-drug operations, with police claiming to have acted in self-defence. Human rights organizations estimate the actual death toll at between 12,000 and 30,000.

    "Duterte's ruthless war on drugs was not simply a campaign against crime; it was a way of governing through killing," David Johnson, a professor of sociology at the University of Hawaii at Manoa, told DW.

    "The extraordinary violence he ordered and encouraged was sustained by a combination of extraordinary problems of impunity in the Philippine criminal justice system and deep failures of democracy in that country,” Johnson noted.

    "These conditions made extrajudicial killing politically useful even though it was ineffective as crime control," he added.

    Duterte also used state power to intimidate and suppress wide sections of Philippine society, including opposition politicians, civil society groups, journalists, lawyers and judges, Diane Desierto, a professor of law and global affairs at the University of Notre Dame, told DW.

    The deterioration of human rights under Duterte damaged the Philippines' international standing and strained relations with its traditional Western partners, particularly the United States under President Barack Obama and the European Union, which threatened to withdraw Manila's preferential trade privilege.

    According to recent reports, duterte left office in June 2022 as one of the most popular presidents in recent Philippine history. A survey conducted by pollster Social Weather Stations found that 88% of Filipinos were satisfied with his performance.

    His daughter was overwhelmingly elected vice president in May 2022, while their allies dominated that year's Senate elections.

    "Up to now, the Dutertes remain popular not in spite of the drug war but because of it,” Arguelles said.

    Despite years of domestic and international scrutiny, Duterte remained at liberty for nearly three years after leaving office.

    The ICC opened a preliminary examination into the drug war in 2018, prompting Duterte to withdraw the Philippines from the court's founding treaty. A formal investigation began in September 2021.

    For much of his early presidency, President Ferdinand Marcos refused to cooperate with the ICC investigation.

    What changed was the breakdown of relations between the Marcoses and the Dutertes, two of the country's most powerful political dynasties.

    Marcos' father had ruled the Philippines as a dictator until he was overthrown in the 1986 People Power Revolution.

    To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

    In a recent development, the alliance that brought Marcos Jr. and Sara Duterte to power in 2022 unravelled spectacularly after November 2024, when the vice president claimed she had arranged for Marcos to be assassinated in the event of her own killing. She has since faced successive impeachment efforts.

    Philippine authorities arrested Rodrigo Duterte in March 2025, acting on an ICC arrest warrant issued four days earlier.

    In April this year, ICC judges confirmed three charges of crimes against humanity involving murder and attempted murder.

    The trial will begin with opening statements, followed by testimony from prosecution witnesses. The process is expected to be extensive, potentially running until 2028, the year of the next Philippine presidential elections.

    The Philippines is effectively confronting two different questions about the Duterte legacy: whether Rodrigo Duterte should be held criminally accountable for his presidency and whether his family should be entrusted with political power again, Arguelles said.

    Duterte-aligned senators implicated in the ICC investigation could face arrest and transfer to The Hague, while Sara Duterte is still a leading contender for the 2028 presidency, despite an ongoing impeachment trial over allegations of unexplained wealth that could see her barred from public office.

    Her brother, Sebastian Duterte, the mayor of Davao City, has also become a possible alternative presidential candidate.

    To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

    By portraying the ICC proceedings as foreign interference and political persecution, the Duterte family hopes to preserve the political capital accumulated during Rodrigo Duterte's presidency, Jayson Lamchek, a legal scholar at Western Sydney University, told DW.

    Before her father's arrest, Sara Duterte's performance and trust ratings had been declining amid allegations that she had misused confidential government funds.

    However, her ratings rebounded following his detention and have largely held up despite the ongoing impeachment controversies, Ronald Holmes, a political science professor at De La Salle University and president of polling firm Pulse Asia Research, told DW.

    "A conviction or prolonged trial near election season will likely turn the 2028 vote into a direct referendum on the Duterte legacy, either rallying sympathetic voters against perceived foreign and domestic persecution or galvanizing opposition forces around demands for accountability," Holmes stated.

    For many Filipinos, however, the trial's significance goes well beyond the political rivalry between the two dynasties.

    "Rodrigo Duterte's trial in the ICC is a milestone not only for the victims and families of the war on drugs but for the entire country," Jean Encinas-Franco, a professor of political science at the University of the Philippines Diliman, told DW.

    Sources indicate that "Duterte and his cabal ruled by fear and misogyny and held Filipinos under his iron grip. The Filipino people deserve an answer. The Filipino people deserve justice," she added.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Watch: Taylor on the 'overwhelming reaction' to Duran Duran's music.
    • Simon Le Bon, Sir Rod Stewart and Gary Kemp are among the pop stars who have paid tribute to Duran Duran guitarist Andy Taylor following his death at the age of 65.
    • Taylor co-wrote some of the group's biggest hits including Save A Prayer, Rio and Girls On Film.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Watch: Taylor on the 'overwhelming reaction' to Duran Duran's music.

    Simon Le Bon, Sir Rod Stewart and Gary Kemp are among the pop stars who have paid tribute to Duran Duran guitarist Andy Taylor following his death at the age of 65.

    Taylor co-wrote some of the group's biggest hits including Save A Prayer, Rio and Girls On Film.

    Le Bon and his bandmates paid tribute, saying "he brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music", while Sir Rod remembered his "dear pal" and Spandau Ballet's Kemp called him "a great player who set the tone for the 80s".

    Taylor's wife Tracey called him "the rock of our family", adding: "We will miss him every single day." He died after "a long and courageous battle with prostate cancer", Duran Duran noted in a statement on Wednesday.

    Andy Taylor: Duran Duran's livewire guitarist who was a Wild Boy on stage and off.

    He died "peacefully at home, surrounded by his family, on Monday 23rd November", a statement said.

    Paying tribute, his Duran Duran bandmates remarked: "From the moment he arrived in Birmingham from the North East with a guitar and an unshakeable belief in what we could become, he brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music.

    "His playing drove the songs that took us around the world, and with a dry wit that was matched only by his wonderfully unsentimental, no-nonsense outlook on life he kept us grounded and gave the band its edge through the extraordinary years that followed.".

    They said their thoughts were with his wife, children and grandson.

    Le Bon mentioned there was a "a massive Andy Taylor shaped hole in my heart".

    "Andy never took the easy musical route. His overdrive overdrove us into being the only funk/rock/punk band in the New Romantic movement, with songs that still survive, decades later.".

    Watch: Andy Taylor tells the BBC about his cancer diagnosis in 2023.

    Sir Rod, who wrote five songs with Taylor for the 1988 album Out of Order, recalled them making "some good music together" and having "some outrageous fun".

    Kemp said Taylor "influenced many of us along the way with his sparse staccato style", adding: "He brought shameless rock to the mix.".

    In a band tribute, Spandau Ballet called him "a hugely talented musician and an crucial part of the British music scene".

    US guitarist Nile Rodgers, the co-founder of Chic, recalled "countless great days and nights" with his "dear friend".

    Belinda Carlisle said she was "blessed" to have worked with Taylor, who played the guitar solo and was in the video for her song Mad About You.

    Former Led Zeppelin frontman Robert Plant called Taylor "a tough fighter", while Then Jerico's Mark Shaw remembered him as "one of the greatest musicians and songwriters I've ever heard and had the privilege to work with".

    Taylor (second left) married his wife Tracey at the Chateau Marmont hotel in Los Angeles in 1982.

    Taylor's wife Tracey, a hairstylist he met during the early days of Duran Duran, and whom he married in 1982, remarked: "For all the incredible experiences music brought him, family always came first for Taylor, adding: "Nothing made him happier than having us all together.".

    She stated he faced the last few years "with so much courage and determination" and said they were "grateful" for the "kindness and support shown to him by fans throughout his illness", saying it brought him "immense comfort and strength".

    Andy Taylor's guitar riffs powered some of Duran Duran's best-known songs.

    The son of a fisherman, Taylor taught himself guitar, bass, and drums and began playing professionally at age 13.

    He played with several bands around the UK before answering a music paper advertisement for a "live-wire guitarist", which led to his audition for Duran Duran in Birmingham in April 1980.

    The group went on to achieve global fame through the Latest Romantic movement, which combined slick, melodic synth-pop with aspirational music videos and chiselled good looks.

    Taylor's guitar lines - full of glassy, powerful riffs - were often a highlight of their songs, from the choppy opening of Girls on Film to the sleazy scuzz of Hungry Like The Wolf.

    Duran Duran bridged the sounds of pop, funk, disco, punk and newly introduced wave with a sound that remains indelibly tied to the 1980s.

    Duran Duran were one of the biggest pop acts of the 1980s, and its five members became global hearththrobs.

    Their indelible hooks and airbrushed music videos found a natural home on the newly debuted MTV, giving their career a huge boost in the US.

    They became so popular in the US that the press labeled them the leaders of a "second British invasion" of the charts - alongside groups like Spandau Ballet, Human League and Eurythmics.

    During a hiatus in 1984, Andy and John Taylor enlisted Robert Palmer for their successful but short-lived side project the Power Station.

    The following year, the guitarist decided to quit Duran Duran after a miserable experience performing at Live Aid.

    "We'd reached rock bottom and we had absolutely nothing to say to each other," he wrote in his autobiography, Wild Boy.

    "We drove to the venue through streets packed with excited rock fans, but inside the bus the atmosphere was as if we were on a way to a funeral.".

    He went on to play on Palmer's Addicted To Love, and released a solo album, Thunder, in 1987.

    Taylor quit Duran Duran at the height of their fame in 1985, but rejoined the band several times in the 2000s and contributed to their most recent album, Danse Macabre.

    After a period writing and producing albums for other artists, he rejoined Duran Duran in 2000, lasting for just one album (2004's Astronaut) before parting ways again.

    In 2022, when the band were inducted to the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, Taylor was notably absent from the ceremony, despite public aims for a reunion.

    When the group took the stage, Le Bon read a letter from the guitarist, in which he revealed his diagnosis with stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer.

    Nonetheless, he contributed to the following year's Halloween-themed album Danse Macabre, marking his final collaboration with the band.

    The following BBC programmes will pay tribute to Taylor:.

    Duran Duran at the BBC, on BBC Four on Friday 27 November at 21:30 GMT.

    Sounds of the 80s, on Radio 2 on Saturday 28 November at at 18:00 GMT.

    • According to a Wednesday report by Fortune, citing people familiar with the discussions, Amazon and Meta have held multiple rounds of talks about the matter.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that amazon may be having a change of heart about Meta’s AI agent, Muse. The two tech giants are reportedly discussing a potential deal that would allow Meta’s popular AI agent to connect directly to Amazon’s store.

    The talks would mark a significant reversal from just two months ago, when Muse owners discovered they were unable to purchase products on Amazon and instead received an error message when attempting to check out.

    According to a Wednesday report by Fortune, citing people familiar with the discussions, Amazon and Meta have held multiple rounds of talks about the matter. Two key issues remain under negotiation: how search results would be presented and how advertising would be handled under a potential agreement.

    One of Amazon’s biggest concerns is how third-party shopping agents like Muse could affect its advertising business. In October, Amazon CEO Andy Jassy argued that few customers were making purchases through outside shopping agents.

    Amazon may also have been waiting for Muse to mature before agreeing to integrate it with its marketplace. If Muse places the wrong order or creates a problem with a purchase, Amazon could ultimately be left dealing with frustrated customers and unhappy sellers.

    Fortune reported that executives are concerned that third-party shopping agents could weaken Amazon’s direct relationship with consumers, according to people familiar with the matter.

    Any potential agreement between Amazon and Meta would reportedly require approval from both companies’ CEOs, Fortune also reported.

    Meta and Amazon have not yet responded to TechCrunch’s requests for comment.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that black Friday is officially here, and plenty of great deals are live. Several walking pads are right now marked down, and with winter coming, now is the ideal time to take advantage of the discount. I, for one, have already started prepping my hibernation cave by stocking happy lights, arts and crafts, and a brand-newly introduced walking pad.

    Industry observers note that by the time December arrives, stepping outside might feel like taking a cold plunge. At that point, you’ll wish you had snagged a walking pad sooner to help you reach your step count goals without risking frostbite. Below, get a curated list of walking pad treadmills I have tested and vetted that are on sale.

    Updated November 27, 2026: More walking pad and running treadmill deals were added. Prices and links were also updated.

    Recent findings suggest that the Urevo CyberPad is my favorite walking pad, and it’s on sale for $390 ($110 off). I’m confident in the product’s durability, mainly due to its sturdy-feeling build and comfortable belt. It offers a 14-percent incline, which is one of the highest available in walking pads, and the speed tops out at 4 mph. Unfortunately, the incline capability makes the machine difficult to store under furniture. It weighs about 71 pounds, so moving it around isn’t fun, but the wheels help. You can control the CyberPad with its remote control and companion app. You can also view your real-time metrics on the machine’s display.

    Sources indicate that the Urevo Strol 2S Pro is also on sale for $210 off. This 2-in-1 doubles as a treadmill with adjustable handrails, a display, and an attachable tablet holder. It was simple to set up, complete with a remote control and intuitive companion app. It feels super stable underfoot, even at top speed and incline level (7.6 mph and 9 percent). That top speed likely isn’t fast enough if you’re looking to sprint, but it’s plenty for a good workout. The machine is unobtrusive, has a quiet motor, and the 43-inch track is compact enough to place under your desk. Overall, it’s a sturdy walking pad treadmill that offers great value and range.

    Industry observers note that the WalkingPad C2 Foldable Walking Treadmill’s track is 32.5 inches when folded (and unfurls to 57 inches), making it a great option for storage in small spaces. It weighs 62 pounds, which isn’t light, but it makes for a sturdier running deck and a (hopefully) longer lifespan. You can adjust the speed via the remote control or companion app. Reviewer Kristin Canning found the app itself to be a little wonky. For example, if you don’t start a workout within the app, your data won’t sync. The app also saves each walking session separately, so if you take a break, you start from zero again. The good news is you don’t need to use the app to use the walking pad.

    It has been revealed that canning also didn’t like that when you first start using the machine, you have to walk at slower speeds before you can unlock the upper end of the range. This might appeal to folks who enjoy gamifying their workouts, though. The app also offers workout programs that auto-adjust the speed to your pace via sensors under the belt.

    Here are some more Black Friday discounts on walking pads and treadmills I’ve tested and recommend.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Transitional President Gen Horta N'Tam mentioned the postponement was driven by factors including final reasons.
    • Guinea-Bissau's military rulers have postponed elections scheduled for next week by two years, delaying the return to civilian rule.
    • Transitional President Gen Horta N'Tam revealed in a decree that the presidential and parliamentary elections, originally due on 6 December, would now take place on 26 November 2028.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Transitional President Gen Horta N'Tam mentioned the postponement was driven by factors including final reasons.

    Guinea-Bissau's military rulers have postponed elections scheduled for next week by two years, delaying the return to civilian rule.

    Transitional President Gen Horta N'Tam revealed in a decree that the presidential and parliamentary elections, originally due on 6 December, would now take place on 26 November 2028.

    The announcement came exactly a year after the military seized power, promising to return the country to civilian rule within 12 months.

    In a statement, the presidency said an assessment of electoral preparations had found that there were insufficient "technical, material and financial conditions" to hold the polls as planned.

    It noted the delay would provide more time to ensure the elections were credible, transparent and inclusive, with all candidates given equal opportunities.

    The presidency also reiterated its commitment to holding the country's first-ever local government elections but gave no date for the vote.

    Gen N'Tam was sworn in as transitional president a day after the military overthrew President Umaro Sissoco EmbalÃ³ in November 2025.

    The coup took place three days after general elections and a day before provisional results were due to be announced.

    Both EmbalÃ³ and his main challenger, Fernando Dias, had claimed victory.

    EmbalÃ³, who has since been living in exile in Morocco, was barred from returning to Guinea-Bissau last month, despite expressing an interest in contesting the elections.

    Guinea-Bissau has experienced several coups and attempted coups since gaining independence from Portugal in 1974.

    Todoist confirms 6% of customers’ details were stolen in data breach

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (518 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, task management app Todoist said on Tuesday that a hacker gained access to its production systems and stole customer data, including email IDs, password hashes, and account creation dates.
    • Todoist mentioned the attacker used stolen credentials to access the company’s version control system and source code between November 22 and 23.
    • The hacker downloaded credentials of early Todoist consumers whose passwords were stored using an older hashing method, but didn’t change any source code, the manufacturer noted.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, task management app Todoist said on Tuesday that a hacker gained access to its production systems and stole customer data, including email IDs, password hashes, and account creation dates. The organization said around 6% of its customers were affected and blamed stolen credentials for the breach.

    Todoist mentioned the attacker used stolen credentials to access the company’s version control system and source code between November 22 and 23. The hacker then changed employee access controls and reached the app’s cloud infrastructure via an employee’s work account.

    The hacker downloaded credentials of early Todoist consumers whose passwords were stored using an older hashing method, but didn’t change any source code, the manufacturer noted. Todoist said it has blocked the attack path and reset passwords as a mitigation step, as well as disabled the Todoist for Outlook email add-on.

    For a small number of people, about 0.001% of its userbase, the hacker also searched through tasks, comments, and attachment names to look for credentials for other services, like API keys and access tokens.

    The hacker also pulled Todoist API tokens and Slack integration tokens, and looked for emails, addresses, and attachment file names through the Todoist for Outlook extension if it was connected to accounts and had permission to read emails.

    Industry observers note that the organization stated it has sent a notice to those affected and asked them to reset their credentials and change their login details in other places with the same password. The company is asking people to also revision API tokens, reconnect integrations, and revoke or replace any access keys, recovery phrases, or credentials they had stored in Todoist comments.

    Todoist remarked it has also reset its internal access structure and how remote command execution works in its cloud environment to prevent such incidents in the future.

    Todoist’s founder and CEO Amir Salihefendić apologized to users about the incident on X, and remarked the tech giant will take a closer look at why it happened.

    The to-do app’s data breach is the latest in a burgeoning list of data breaches in which hackers use stolen credentials to access data and systems at enterprises. So far this year, we’ve seen several companies fall victim to this form of attack, including Uber and Klue.

    #151567. Google search alternative Kagi introduces Gmail rival

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (569 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

    Google search alternative Kagi introduces Gmail rival

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (569 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, kagi, a small, Palo Alto, California-based software organization that provides a subscription-based search engine as an alternative to Google, has released a Gmail-like e-mail service.
    • Additionally, Kagi is rolling out a calendar as part of the mail service.
    • The email interface, presently in public beta, is minimalist.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, kagi, a small, Palo Alto, California-based software organization that provides a subscription-based search engine as an alternative to Google, has released a Gmail-like e-mail service. Dubbed Kagi Mail, it makes many of the same claims as the search engine product: privacy, personal data sovereignty, customization, and control.

    Additionally, Kagi is rolling out a calendar as part of the mail service. Right now, both the email and calendar interfaces are web-only, but native Android and iOS apps are planned for the fourth quarter of next year.

    The email interface, presently in public beta, is minimalist. It emphasizes keyboard commands, as well as a private and ad-free experience. (You can see more details in Kagi’s blog post about what they mean by private.) Other feature offerings include unlimited aliases and domains, an anti-lock-in policy for user data, 50GB of storage, rule-based filtering with Sieve, an MCP server, and several optional, off-by-default AI features, like chatting with an agent to search email history, do large-scale re-labeling, or define additional filtering rules.

    It has been revealed that some major features are still missing, though. As noted, there are no native apps yet. Critically, there is no contacts address book, but that is also coming in 2027 (Q1 in this case) according to the roadmap.

    Recent findings suggest that like the search engine, Kagi Mail is a paid service. It’s not included in the $5 per month basic Kagi plan, nor is it in the $10 per month unlimited search plan. It is, however, included in the $25 per month Kagi Ultimate subscription, which also offers frontier AI models.

    Recent findings suggest that that’s a lot to pay for email when Gmail has historically been such a strong product. To most people, it seems ridiculous to imagine paying for a subscription, and that’s understandable.

    Sources indicate that kagi also argues that Google’s search results—and increasingly its email as well—are polluted or corrupted by ad sales incentives. On that, several Ars staffers agree—my colleague Lee Hutchinson wrote at length about why he ditched Google Search for Kagi a year ago. A couple other Ars staffers have since made the same move, myself included—but to be fair, search is a very big part of our day-to-day work, and that’s not true to the same degree for everybody.

    Industry observers note that the pitch for email is a little harder, because most people probably don’t perceive as much impact of Google’s business incentives on Gmail. That has maybe changed recently, as Google has begun inserting Gemini into Gmail aggressively, but Kagi has AI features, too—the difference is that they’re generally more conservative and sensible. (You can disable either Gemini in Gmail or Kagi’s AI features in Kagi Mail, too.).

    Recent findings suggest that email is also different because there are already more direct competitors to Kagi Mail. The most popular in this category is Proton Mail, which goes even further on privacy and security with end-to-end encryption, but that organization is embroiled in controversies right now. There’s also Tuta, which Kagi specifically flags and praises in its blog post as a good existing alternative.

    Based on a few hours of use, Kagi Mail seems like it’s going in the right direction, but it will need refinement to permanently unseat Gmail. Your needs may vary, but there are many good reasons to consider alternatives to Google’s business model and products.

    #151562. Uganda to withdraw troops from DR Congo town amid diplomatic row

    📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (591 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

    Uganda to withdraw troops from DR Congo town amid diplomatic row

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (591 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The planned withdrawal will end Uganda's nearly two-year campaign against ADF militants in Lubero.
    • Uganda has revealed looks to withdraw its troops from a town in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo within two weeks, as diplomatic tensions escalate between the two neighbours.
    • The troops will hand over security in Lubero, in North Kivu province, to Congolese forces after nearly two years of military operations, the Ugandan army said in a statement on Friday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The planned withdrawal will end Uganda's nearly two-year campaign against ADF militants in Lubero.

    Uganda has revealed looks to withdraw its troops from a town in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo within two weeks, as diplomatic tensions escalate between the two neighbours.

    The troops will hand over security in Lubero, in North Kivu province, to Congolese forces after nearly two years of military operations, the Ugandan army said in a statement on Friday.

    The announcement comes days after DR Congo summoned Uganda's top diplomat in Kinshasa over controversial social media posts by Uganda's military chief, Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, who is the son of President Yoweri Museveni.

    The Ugandan military did not give a reason for the withdrawal or say whether it was linked to the diplomatic row.

    What are Ugandan forces doing in DR Congo?

    The Uganda People's Defence Forces (UPDF) were deployed to Lubero to pursue fighters from the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) Islamist group fleeing joint military operations elsewhere in eastern DR Congo.

    The ADF, which originated in Uganda in the 1990s, is affiliated to the Islamic State and has been blamed for numerous deadly attacks on civilians in both countries.

    Uganda first deployed troops to eastern DR Congo under the current joint military campaign in November 2021, following a series of bomb attacks in the Ugandan capital, Kampala.

    Ugandan army spokesperson Col Chris Magezi said that the joint military campaign, known as Operation Shujaa, would continue elsewhere in DR Congo.

    The planned withdrawal applies only to Lubero town.

    Five years into the joint offensive, the ADF remains DR Congo's deadliest armed group, despite a significant decline in its activities in Uganda, according to the conflict monitoring organisation Armed Conflict Location & Event Data (Acled).

    John Ngono, Acled's DR Congo analyst, said the group was killing an average of four civilians a day and had expanded into previously unaffected parts of eastern DR Congo.

    He said the findings suggested that "Operation Shujaa may have improved security in Uganda while shifting the geographical impact of violence within the DRC".

    Acled states the group has not carried out an attack in Uganda since June 2025, but its growing interest in mineral resources in DR Congo could help finance its operations and sustain its ability to threaten both countries.

    The planned withdrawal comes amid strained relations between Uganda and DR Congo, despite years of close military co-operation.

    Earlier this week, Gen Kainerugaba appeared to endorse a rebel takeover of Walikale, a mineral-rich territory in eastern DR Congo, threatening that Ugandan troops would seize it themselves if the rebels failed to do so.

    The Congolese foreign ministry described his remarks as "particularly serious" and demanded that Uganda clarify its official position and take steps to prevent similar incidents.

    Gen Kainerugaba also defended Uganda's military presence in eastern DR Congo, insisting it was driven by security concerns.

    The planned withdrawal comes amid renewed fighting between Congolese forces and rebels in the wider Lubero territory, raising fresh concerns about the safety of civilians.

    Eastern DR Congo has endured decades of conflict involving dozens of armed groups, with millions of people forced to flee their homes.

    • insurer Allstate has been experiencing a tech outage since Monday morning, leaving customers nationwide unable to access their accounts, review their policy information, file claims, pay their bills, and more, just ahead of the U.S.
    • The outage has been impacting both the company’s website and mobile app, TechCrunch confirmed.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that U.S. insurer Allstate has been experiencing a tech outage since Monday morning, leaving customers nationwide unable to access their accounts, review their policy information, file claims, pay their bills, and more, just ahead of the U.S. Thanksgiving holidays.

    The outage has been impacting both the company’s website and mobile app, TechCrunch confirmed.

    Sources indicate that the breakdown follows a report from earlier this month that Allstate was planning to lay off up to 10% of its staff as part of an AI-driven efficiency push. (The manufacturer had not confirmed the report, which was attributed to unnamed sources.).

    Allstate’s outage is the latest in a series of disruptions to services such as Microsoft Outlook and Teams, the airlines, Apple Pay, and several banks. Trump administration officials have said the outages are not being caused by cyberattacks, but are rather being caused by a recent set of upgrades to systems, many of which run on older technology. Those systems are now in need of more frequent security and bug fixes as AI makes it easier and faster to discover vulnerabilities.

    Downdetector, a crowdsourced outage-reporting website, demonstrates consumers began reporting Allstate’s outage from Monday morning. However, the company hasn’t yet issued a formal statement about the disruption, what’s causing it, or when it may be resolved. In the meantime, local insurance agents have been fielding calls and emails from customers who aren’t able to use the company’s online services.

    Industry observers note that the timing of the outage is particularly bad given that Thanksgiving is a massive travel holiday in the U.S., which means there will be car accidents. Customers will be left without a way to get in touch with their auto insurer to file claims and get roadside assistance through Allstate’s app.

    Allstate did not immediately return a request for comment. On Wednesday evening, after publication, the manufacturer sent the following statement (below). It did not answer questions about the outage’s cause or planned resolution.

    Allstate customers can reach us in many ways, including online, by phone and through local offices. Some access has been restricted over the last 48 hours, but we continue to be available for customers and respond to and settle claims. To the extent service interruptions impact a customer’s ability to make a payment, they won’t lose coverage or be charged late fees.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Emmanuel Macron said it would be a "strategic mistake" to reduce EU spending.

    European Union (EU) leaders have deferred negotiations on its long-term budget after tensions surfaced over the bloc's spending priorities and aid for Ukraine.

    Tense talks on the 2028-34 budget ended after 12 hours on Thursday at a summit in Brussels, with some members walking out of negotiations that will resume in December.

    Divisions were largely split along the lines of countries, including France and Italy, wanting to approve a higher-spending proposal against those advocating for financial restraint, with Germany chief among them.

    Many members want the budget locked in ahead of several high-stakes elections held across Europe in 2027, including in France.

    Countries remain divided over a proposal to provide Ukraine with an additional loan of â¬45bn (Â£37.6bn), split between non-military and military funding.

    Slovakia, the Czech Republic and Hungary have objected to the loan, but German Chancellor Frederich Merz said uniform EU agreement was a condition for approving the broader budget.

    "I stand by my view that aid for Ukraine must be supported by the European Union as a whole," Merz told reporters.

    "The European Union comprises of 27 member states, not 23 or 24.".

    Bulgaria, which previously opposed the plan, said it would agree to fund part of the loan that commits non-military financial support to Kyiv, marking a small sign of progress emerging from the special summit of the European Council.

    EU members have been wrangling over the long-term budget after the European Commission submitted a â¬2tn proposal earlier this year, with some countries objecting to high levels of spending.

    Those advocating higher spending want the funds to future-proof industries such as farming and invest in regional development. Fiscally cautious countries want to avoid amassing ballooning debt.

    Thursday's talks were set up by the European Council to unblock the impasse, with a proposal to reduce spending by approximately â¬220bn to â¬230bn.

    Under the current proposal, the budget totals â¬1.582tn, which includes â¬140bn to repay pandemic-era borrowing.

    Four countries wanting to rein in the budget, including Denmark and Austria, walked out of negotiations after several hours of meetings.

    Merz said there was "upcoming movement" towards reducing the size of the EU budget, though he added "we are not there yet" when he confirmed that a new round of negotiations would not take place in Brussels on Friday.

    European budgets requires approval from all 27 countries, with each country effectively holding veto power.

    French President Emmanuel Macron said it would be a "strategic mistake" to lower long-term spending.

    France's forthcoming presidential election came into focus during the EU budget talks, with frontrunner Marine Le Pen calling the talks an "underhanded political manoeuvring to thwart the democratic will of the French people".

    Last month, Le Pen confirmed she would significantly reduce French aid to Ukraine and EU contributions if she were to win the presidency.

    Macron addressed Le Pen's remarks on the sidelines of the Brussels summit, saying: "It is an odd kind of arrogance to behave as if she is already in charge of France's destiny because, as things stand, she has not been elected.".

    Once the talks concluded, the European Council confirmed a two-day summit on 17 and 18 December would revive budget negotiations.

    Spanish economist Pablo HernÃ¡ndez de Cos was also named as the next President of the European Central Bank, replacing Christine Lagarde from February 2027.

    The app’s latest update will turn half the display into a keyboard for tiny typing.

    Sources indicate that edovia's Screens is a remote desktop app, which gives you a way to control your computer for the iPhone, iPad, another Mac or even the Vision Pro. Screens 5.10.6, its latest enhancement, adds the ability to turn your iPhone Duo into a tiny MacBook when it's in a partially open, clamshell configuration. When the phone is folded halfway, you can use the app's upcoming Laptop Mode to display your remote desktop on the upper half of the screen and a keyboard with trackpad below.

    In a recent development, its keyboard supports multiple languages, and you can swipe down on keys to see alternative characters like you can on the iPad. The trackpad supports Screens' gestures. Of course, they're not a complete replacement for actual physical keyboards and trackpads, but they could be good enough to use in a pinch, or even regularly if you're used to typing on a screen or don't need to type anything lengthy.

    The iPhone Duo's form factor is so unlike previous iPhones that we'd love to see more fun ways developers can use it to create unique experiences for the device's people. Some developers, however, might not find it that easy: Instagram's Adam Mosseri recently said that it will be "pretty challenging" to design Instagram "in a way that feels great" for the device.

    • The feature is rolling out globally to all consumers across iOS and Android.
    • Industry observers note that customers will be able to see all their scheduled messages and delete them if needed.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    WhatsApp on Wednesday started rolling out a much-sought-after feature: the ability to schedule messages in both individual and group chats.

    The feature is rolling out globally to all consumers across iOS and Android. Once it becomes available, you can type a message and long-press the send button to schedule it. You can choose to send a message anywhere between 10 minutes and 14 days later.

    Industry observers note that customers will be able to see all their scheduled messages and delete them if needed. It’s not clear if there is a way to edit the schedule of a message.

    Notably, scheduled messages will be sent even if your phone is off or outside network coverage. You can schedule messages containing text, photos, and videos.

    It has been revealed that the feature could prove useful for wishing someone a happy birthday on time or chatting with people across time zones. Businesses may also find it easier to schedule texts and updates to their customers, and people who use the app to coordinate work will likely find themselves using scheduled texts to update their teams.

    WhatsApp rivals like Telegram and Signal have had the ability to schedule messages for a while now, so the Meta-owned chat app is late in rolling it out.

    Industry News: On the arrest of Informer TV owner and editor-in-chief Dragan J. Vucicevic: Has the reckoning with Serbia's pro-Vucic media machine begun?

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1065 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Break their ribs," shouted the man in the studio during a live TV broadcast.
    • According to recent reports, the man in question was Dragan J.
    • On November 25, Vucicevic was arrested by the police on suspicion of causing panic and disorder and obstructing justice.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    "Beat them! Break their ribs," shouted the man in the studio during a live TV broadcast.

    According to recent reports, the man in question was Dragan J. Vucicevic, editor-in-chief of the channel Informer TV, and he was urging police officers to use force against demonstrators during a major student protest in June last year.

    On November 25, Vucicevic was arrested by the police on suspicion of causing panic and disorder and obstructing justice. According to the authorities, his appearances "created an atmosphere of public lynching" and he labelled 97 citizens as enemies of the state.

    The authorities cite instances where he described protesters as "scum," "hyenas" and "vultures" and spread claims that the students were preparing a "bloodbath" and a "civil war.".

    To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

    The prosecution notes that between 2023 and 2026, Vucicevic systematically used Informer TV to conduct a campaign that incited hatred and targeted political opponents of the previous government, activists and independent journalists.

    Vucicevic's arrest comes at a time of profound political change in Serbia.

    Following the Student List's victory in the parliamentary election in late October and the end of the Serbian Progressive Party's (SNS) 14-year rule, questions have arisen about the accountability of people who were part of the previous political and institutional system.

    Critics have described Vucicevic as the mouthpiece of former President Aleksandar Vucic — a man who said publicly what the president was thinking but could not say himself because of the office he held.

    Industry observers note that "He [Vucicevic] is someone who stopped being a journalist a long time ago, and I think he crossed the line of being merely a propagandist some time ago. He was, in fact, a weapon in the hands of Aleksandar Vucic and his party," said Ivana Stevanovic of the Slavko Curuvija Foundation, a Belgrade-based organization named after a Serbian journalist who was killed in 1999 that provides media support and fights for press freedom.

    Stevanovic told DW that Vucicevic used his media platforms to "target and endanger people, spread falsehoods that threatened their safety," all as part of a campaign against political opponents, journalists and media outlets who were critical of the government's record.

    Industry observers note that "This man revealed a female student's intimate photographs live on air. He stalked people. He had his notorious 'Viewer Intelligence Service,' which secretly followed people and filmed them in their everyday lives, then turned that material into disgusting reports," she said.

    In a recent development, "We had calls for violence, threats and insults against prosecutors who were doing their jobs and judges who were issuing lawful rulings, expressed in indescribable language. We had wiretapping, recordings of conversations in restaurants presented as conspiracies to overthrow the state. Media outlets and journalists were accused of plotting to assassinate the president, while their reporting was portrayed as treason and selling out Kosovo," she told DW, adding that "the entire television channel is one big criminal offence.".

    The Regulatory Authority for Electronic Media (REM) has already issued several warnings and temporarily halted the broadcasting of certain programs on Informer TV.

    Journalists' and media associations, civil society organizations and representatives of academia have released an initiative to have the channel's broadcasting license revoked.

    According to the Slavko Curuvija Foundation, more than 1,000 court cases concerning the protection of reputation and honor have been brought against Informer in recent years.

    Industry observers note that "Of the cases concluded over the past three years, courts upheld the claims in 92% of them," stated Stevanovic. "Compensation was awarded to people whose rights had been violated. Informer even paid damages to the same individuals several times for the same lies, which it kept publishing about them. None of these financial penalties made them stop.".

    On one occasion, Dragan J. Vucicevic himself asked REM to impose a financial penalty on him rather than ban part of his program.

    Money, it seems, was not a problem for Insajder Tim, the organization behind all Informer media platforms (a daily tabloid newspaper, a television channel and an online portal).

    According to an investigation by Raskrikavanje, a fact-checking website that monitors the output of Serbian media, Insajder Tim, received around €273,000 ($299,000) in public funds in 2024 alone through public procurement contracts, advertising and media project funding.

    Representatives of the Student List have claimed that the state-owned telecommunications tech giant Telekom Srbija paid Informer between €500,000 and €700,000 a month.

    Telekom Srbija, which also owns a cable network distributing television channels to millions of users in Serbia, cited business confidentiality when asked about the details of its cooperation with Informer.

    Vucicevic and his lawyers reject the accusations.

    The defense argues that the proceedings amount to punishing someone for words they have spoken and raise questions about the boundary between freedom of expression and criminal liability.

    Former President Aleksandar Vucic mentioned Vucicevic had been arrested solely because of his journalistic work. SNS lawmakers walked out of a parliamentary session following news of the arrest and gathered outside the police station where the Informer editor was being held.

    Stevanovic maintains that by arresting Vucicevic, Serbia is fulfilling its international obligations, including those arising from the European Convention on Human Rights and international conventions protecting civil and political rights.

    "What constitutes a call for violence and a threat to democracy, security and health must be sanctioned and removed from the public sphere," she said.

    Vucicevic has been remanded in custody for 30 days.

    The offence of causing panic and disorder through the media carries a prison sentence of between six months and five years.

    Stevanovic points out, however, that the outcome of the case is not certain because the executive branch, the police and the Ministry of the Interior formally remain under the control of the outgoing government until such time as the Student List forms a newly introduced cabinet.

    It has been revealed that "What is happening now could be an internal power struggle within their own ranks, or an attempt by some prosecutors to clean up their records and ingratiate themselves with the newly introduced authorities, assuming what their wishes and intentions regarding Informer might be," she remarked. "Or it could be a serious manipulation, a staged arrest designed to portray Serbia abroad as a country carrying out revolutionary terror, which, of course, is not true.".

    European spacecraft finds chaotic scene after asteroid deflection experiment

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1281 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that four years ago, NASA dispatched a small spacecraft on a suicide mission to show how humanity might deflect an asteroid on a collision course with Earth.
    • Using telescopes, astronomers measured changes in the orbit of Dimorphos around a larger asteroid companion named Didymos in the aftermath of NASA’s Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) mission.
    • It has been revealed that but scientists could only learn so much from DART.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that four years ago, NASA dispatched a small spacecraft on a suicide mission to show how humanity might deflect an asteroid on a collision course with Earth. The first-of-its-kind experiment worked beautifully as the solar-powered space probe slammed into asteroid Dimorphos, permanently altering its trajectory.

    Using telescopes, astronomers measured changes in the orbit of Dimorphos around a larger asteroid companion named Didymos in the aftermath of NASA’s Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) mission. The spacecraft released some 10 billion joules of energy as it impacted Dimorphos in September 2022 at more than 13,700 mph (6.14 kilometers per second), shortening the asteroid’s 12-hour orbit around Didymos by about 33 minutes, 25 times the most conservative expectation.

    It has been revealed that but scientists could only learn so much from DART. The collision destroyed the spacecraft, as expected. DART recorded images as it took aim on Dimorphos, but only faraway telescopes and a small CubeSat that briefly detected the impact flash could see what happened next.

    In a recent development, “We knew right away that the impact was successful, that DART made a really, really large mess,” said Sabina Raducan, a planetary scientist at the International Space Science Institute in Bern, Switzerland. “However, we didn’t really know what kind of mess. We were still missing pieces of the puzzle.”.

    The European Space Agency’s Hera spacecraft recently arrived in the vicinity of Didymos and Dimorphos after a two-year journey from a launch pad in Florida. On Wednesday, ESA released Hera’s first views of the scar left by DART on Dimorphos. The images show the car-sized impactor carved out a crater the size of a stadium, nearly as significant as Dimorphos itself, a rugged chunk of extraterrestrial rock measuring about 500 feet (151 meters) across.

    Mission planners selected Didymos and Dimorphos for the deflection experiment because they are similar to many near-Earth asteroids, but there’s no risk of them striking our home planet. Scientists weren’t sure what Hera would find when it got to the double asteroid, presently orbiting the Sun about 120 million miles (193.5 million kilometers) from Earth.

    Industry observers note that “I would say we had two kinds of predictions: either we made a crater, or we reshaped the asteroid,” said Patrick Michel, Hera’s principal investigator from Côte d’Azur Observatory in Nice, France. “In fact, we did both because the crater is so large that the shape has changed. Therefore, we are in a sort of a transition between just cratering and global transformation, and we are still not sure how this can happen.”.

    Sources indicate that hera found Didymos, the larger of the two asteroids, spinning on its axis just as DART observed on final approach in 2022. Dimorphos is no longer so stable.

    “As Hera returned more images, it became clear that the DART impact has left Dimorphos tumbling wildly in its orbit,” claims Michael Kueppers, ESA’s Hera mission scientist.

    Industry observers note that the Hera spacecraft will fly closer to Didymos and Dimorphos over the next six months to obtain more detailed observations. Hera will release two small sub-satellites to attempt landings on Dimorphos and collect data on the asteroid’s composition, internal structure, and mass.

    According to recent reports, scientists will use this information to reconstruct the dynamics of DART’s impact four years ago and better understand how a future deflection mission might move an asteroid off a trajectory that actually threatens Earth. Near-Earth asteroids come in many shapes and sizes, with different densities and makeups, so knowledge of Dimorphos’s physical properties will anchor predictive computer models teaching scientists how best to deflect all types of asteroids.

    “Once we understand, we have a breakthrough, which really solves planetary defense,” Michel mentioned in an interview with Ars.

    In its initial reconnaissance this month, Hera spotted hundreds of boulders surrounding the double asteroid. This was not entirely unexpected. A picture taken by the Hubble Space Telescope shortly after DART’s impact highlighted a cloud of material streaming behind Didymos and Dimorphos, but scientists were astonished by the extent of the debris swarm in Hera’s first images.

    Industry observers note that “As we approached Didymos and Dimorphos, we rapidly realized the asteroids were not alone,” said Naomi Murdoch, planetary scientist at the Institut Supérieur de l’Aéronautique et de l’Espace in Toulouse, France. “In fact, they had a lot of company.”.

    According to recent reports, an image released by ESA on Wednesday combines 11 long exposure frames from Hera’s hyperspectral camera. Image processors on the ground digitally removed the relatively bright Didymos and Dimorphos to reveal a panoply of dimmer streaks and dots, each of which is a rock fragment ranging in size from a football to a washing machine, Murdoch mentioned.

    “Hera came to visit two asteroids, and we found hundreds of companions,” Murdoch said.

    One obvious explanation for the boulders is they were thrown off Dimorphos when DART slammed into it. But scientists cautioned they need more information before they can say that with surety. Hera is the first space mission to undertake a sustained study of an asteroid with its own moon. The debris around the two asteroids might be relics from the creation of Dimorphos some time in the ancient past.

    “Hera will allow us to study that in more detail,” Murdoch stated. “We really need to know more about these boulders and characterize them to understand if they’re linked to DART, if they’re linked to another process, and what the consequences might be for other asteroid systems in the Solar System.”.

    The boulder field will create challenges for navigating around the asteroids. In particular, the boulders are an added risk for the two small CubeSats Hera is supposed to deploy in January.

    It has been revealed that “We saw a couple of images that didn’t reassure me,” noted Margherita Cardi, project manager for the Milani CubeSat. “There is a mix of excitement and panic.”.

    Claudia Balossi, spacecraft systems engineer for Hera’s other CubeSat, named Juventas, said her mission’s planned trajectory would take it right through the boulders as it moves within a couple of miles of the asteroids, then finally toward a landing attempt on Dimorphos, where it will measure the miniature world’s tenuous gravity field.

    “We are right in the middle of it,” Balossi said. “The smallest ones are probably just as substantial as we are and the biggest ones are very big. In the worst case, a boulder will land on us. We will activate our gravimeter right away [if that happens],” Balossi joked.

    The good news is the asteroids’ gravity is so weak that Hera, Milani, Juventas, and the hazards around them all move at snail-like speeds. Hera’s current trajectory takes it around the asteroids at a relative velocity of just a quarter-mile per hour, or about 12 centimeters per second. At that speed, there’s no danger of a sudden catastrophic hypervelocity collision between the spacecraft and the boulders lurking nearby.

    Scientists have seen this at an asteroid before. NASA’s OSIRIS-REx spacecraft kicked up an estimated six tons of rock and dust when it gently moved in to collect a sample from an asteroid named Bennu in 2020. Low gravity and weak surface cohesion are a recipe for outsized effects.

    According to recent reports, “These types of bodies, because of their low gravity, have a very counterintuitive behavior,” Michel said. “Each time we interact with them, whether to take a sample or to make an impact, the response of the surface was not the one we predicted, simply because our intuition relies on what we experience every day on Earth. Even if the rules of physics are the same in the Universe, they express very differently depending on local attraction.”.

Today's sentence reflects our commitment to protecting victims, safeguarding the integrity of our financial markets and holding accountable those who exploit emerging technologies to defraud others.".

    N3on's not exactly a stranger to AI clones of himself, as it happens. Aftermath noted that he tried using a deepfake of himself to keep his Kick stream going around the clock. N3on's likeness was also used in an AI-generated movie that was released a few months ago.
